program_overview.title: React for Teens
program_overview.tagline: The framework behind the interfaces teens live in, learned properly: real JavaScript first, then React the way it is written now, ending deployed.
program_overview.description:
React renders the interfaces of Instagram, Netflix and half the modern web, and it rewards exactly one kind of learner: the one whose JavaScript is real. This live online course for ages 13 to 18 is built on that truth. Three months of genuine foundations, HTML, CSS and JavaScript through the DOM and modern ES6+, then React itself: components, state, hooks, routing, data fetching, styling, forms, and the craft layer of TypeScript, testing and performance that separates tutorial-followers from builders. The final month adds an honest taste of Next.js and ships a deployed capstone at demo day.

Everything deploys: projects go to public URLs from the first phase, and the capstone is a polished, routed, data-driven React application the student can send to anyone. What the course refuses to do is pad: React Native, full-stack backends and framework tours live in our dedicated courses, pointed to honestly, not stapled on as filler weeks.

The pace is honest: nine months at two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice, with two more months in hand when needed. Homework after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest. Real JavaScript, real React, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: JavaScript first, seriously: three months of real foundations, because React punishes weak JavaScript forever
React as it is written now: function components, hooks, and honest data patterns with loading and error states everywhere
The craft layer included: TypeScript, testing and performance, not left for "later"
Everything deploys: public URLs from phase 1, a deployed capstone at the end
Honest scope: React Native and backends are dedicated courses, pointed to truthfully, not filler weeks
Real assessment: weekly homework, monthly mixed reviews, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest

faqs.question: What will my teen build in this React course?
faqs.answer: More than 20 real builds across nine months: styled, deployed pages and JavaScript projects in the foundation phase, then routed, data-driven React applications with honest loading states, typed and tested features in the craft phase, a small Next.js rebuild, and finally a capstone, a complete React application deployed to a public URL and defended at demo day.

faqs.question: How long does it take a teenager to learn React?
faqs.answer: Nine months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice, and a third of that is deliberately spent on JavaScript foundations, because React punishes weak JavaScript forever. The course keeps two more months in hand for students who need them. Courses that jump into React in week one produce students who can follow tutorials and cannot debug them.

faqs.question: How is my teen assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Homework follows every class, each month ends with an assignment that deliberately mixes new questions with earlier topics, every phase closes with an exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Does my teen need to know JavaScript first?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the design: the first three months build HTML, CSS and JavaScript properly, through the DOM and modern ES6+, before a single React component. Teens who already know some JavaScript are placed by a quick check and move faster through the early months.

faqs.question: Does this course cover React Native or backend development?
faqs.answer: Honestly, no, and on purpose. React Native and backend engineering are real disciplines with their own dedicated courses here, and stapling them on as survey weeks would cheat all three subjects. This course makes the React foundation deep; our app development course continues it onto phones, and our full-stack course adds the backend half.

faqs.question: Is React still worth learning?
faqs.answer: Yes: it remains the most-used frontend framework in industry by a wide margin, the concepts it teaches, components, state, unidirectional data, transfer to every alternative, and its ecosystem (Next.js included, which this course tastes honestly) keeps compounding. A teen fluent in React and TypeScript holds a genuinely employable-track skill.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Parents are welcome to sit in.

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small interactive groups with a real instructor, never pre-recorded videos. React errors are famously cryptic for beginners; live eyes on the code is what keeps early frustration from becoming quitting.
